key_insight: Trivalent planar architectures can support scalable lattice surgery for surface-code logical operations with lower overhead than standard four-valent measurement schemes.
engineering_relevance: This reduces qubit and two-qubit-gate requirements in nearest-neighbor hardware, making fault-tolerant quantum processors more practical for planar devices.
method: Developed scalable lattice-surgery circuit constructions for degree-3 planar connectivity.
Compared resource scaling against four-valent measurement-based lattice surgery.
Evaluated logical fidelity with experimentally realistic simulations for a fluxonium-based architecture.
evidence_signal: Simulations indicate up to about a 25% logical-fidelity improvement at code distance 3, alongside O(d) savings in qubits and two-qubit gates.
watch_item: The reported gains are based on realistic simulations and a specific fluxonium architecture, so performance may differ with hardware noise, calibration, and larger code distances.
paper_title: Towards logical entanglement creation in trivalent planar architectures
